.ai/DECISIONS.md:3878:Correct the Lab interpretation of a quantized or stale reading: at the reading's own source time, `reported - bias` equals the world value only for an unquantized numeric signal under this model. With quantum `q`, it differs by at most `q/2` (including ties); it cannot recover an exact world value. A retained reading across a reporting gap describes its earlier source instant and cannot establish the current or hidden world quantity. S2-01b phase 3b corrects the misleading `ObservationView` docstring and avoids an exact-equality claim in Lab UI/copy; no existing observation, profile, or sealed wire byte changes.
.ai/DECISIONS.md:3910:Decision: `D-2026-10-09-s2-publication-gap-and-batch-boundary`. Codex Architect, resolving S2-01c fix re-review R1 and questions-5 in `.agent/architect-S2-batch-answers-2026-10-09.md`. A completed `RUN_VIRTUAL` schedule's `admitted_through` is the last contiguous ordinary-publication boundary. If it is absent or earlier than `world_reached_instant` after a failed pass, a **stored-schedule-only** advance must refuse `PUBLICATION_GAP` before changing either Lab or gateway clock or submitting a due delayed report. The schedule read and Lab UI must show the incomplete ordinary-publication watermark and world-reached instant, not just a generic staging note; the advance answer must expose the typed refusal. A live session may re-drive the missing ordinary boundary while its gateway clock still permits its original instant. If that instant has passed, keep `PUBLICATION_INSTANT_PASSED`, stop later ordinary and delayed admissions for that run, and show the terminal gap; recovery is a new run, not late stamping or a hidden sequence jump. This strengthens, rather than replaces, the earlier rule permitting a delayed report to publish at the next actually admitted boundary or explicit post-run instant when no ordinary gap blocks it.
.ai/DECISIONS.md:3912:Seal the deterministic boundary groups as currently built. An executed `RUN_VIRTUAL` run with no durable schedule is `SCHEDULE_MISSING` on read and advance even if a live session remains; it must not silently regenerate missing state on a later step. Initial schedule creation during the first start, before any gateway submission, remains valid. A not-yet-started run can remain `NO_SCHEDULE`.

.ai/DECISIONS.md:3991:Decision: `D-2026-10-09-pre-s3-evidence-readiness-health`. Codex Architect, resolving a bounded selected-window CapabilityReadiness/SourceHealth contract for all three domains, separate from the still-open broad shared evidence projections; detail in `.agent/architect-pre-S3-answers.md`. CapabilityReadiness uses declared role/rule version, selected Foundation/bindings and **accepted** evidence for a tenant/Site/domain half-open window at `knowledge_at`. Virtual source time is not compared with real server time as physical freshness or network lag. .ai/DECISIONS.md:4011:**Revisions and jobs.** S3 consumes the S2 `dispatch` recompute queue transactionally with a lease/retry, expands an accepted record's affected source-time interval to continuity neighbors, and reruns at a recorded cutoff. Backdated Foundation/binding publication and analytic-model changes enqueue affected windows too. The worker persists an idempotent `AnalyticRun` keyed by Site, analytic/model version, window and input hash, its exact evidence-ID set, and append-only `AssessmentRevision` rows under a stable interval/asset assessment key. Identical input and output produce no new revision; a changed evidence/configuration/model basis appends a new revision while preserving the earlier one and its selected read URL. Projection replacement and job completion occur atomically only for the still-current input/watermark; a newly dirtied overlapping window must remain dirty for another pass, never be lost by a leased worker. Late accepted evidence may change Necessary/Candidate/Indeterminate but never rewrites an earlier revision. The Performance list/detail returns selected revision, rule version, input hash, coverage, evidence IDs, source and analytic watermarks, built time and explicit limitations.
.ai/DECISIONS.md:4013:**Projection status and cutover.** `NO_PENDING_DISPATCH` in the S2 Evidence read means only that no S2 job is outstanding; it is never a current assessment. frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:179:3. **Decide records.** In one Postgres transaction, lock batch row; for each unprocessed ordinal parse strict envelope, verify identity/sequence and referenced mapping/Foundation validity at `source_time`, normalize with the registered as-accepted conversion, and insert acceptance or rejection plus disposition. Unique message key arbitrates concurrent duplicate deliveries. Equal digest is `DUPLICATE`; changed digest is `CONFLICT` and points to first accepted evidence. Update watermark and create/coalesce recompute jobs in the same commit. Chunk a large batch into short committed transactions; receipt exposes `IN_PROGRESS` until all ordinals are durable. A client retries the same batch/bytes and resumes from the persisted watermark. Return a terminal receipt only after all decisions commit.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:183:**Initial API contract:** `POST /api/ingestion/batches` returns terminal `200` receipt or `202 IN_PROGRESS` receipt; `GET /api/ingestion/batches/{id}` returns the same durable state. `409` is reserved for same batch ID/different bytes or registered identity conflict, `422` for malformed contract, `401/403` for authentication/authorization. Normal reads use `GET /api/sites/{id}/evidence`, `/evidence/records/{id}`, `/overview`, `/performance/{view}`, `/findings/{id}` with `from`, `to` and optional `revision_id`; list reads paginate by stable `(source_time,id)` or `(created_at,id)` cursor. All responses include scope/window, revision IDs, evidence coverage and projection watermark. The UI treats a lagging projection as pending, not healthy. Lab Commit calls this same HTTP boundary with a registered simulated gateway; no privileged product-write endpoint exists.

# Architect rulings: S4-02 batch (2026-10-14)

Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, the S4-02a/b packets and fresh reviews. S4-02a/b and the conditional owner checkpoint remain accepted; these rulings identify follow-on work and the precise registry boundary.

## Q1 â€” SUCCESSION at the current assignment's start

**Permit it.** The packet says the single open-ended assignment containing `valid_from` may be succeeded; a half-open assignment contains its start. Require `valid_from >= recorded_at`, the expected prior revision, one overlapping open-ended assignment, and the existing authorization/idempotency checks. At equality, close the old assignment's recorded-time tenure and insert only the new assignment for `[valid_from, âˆž)`; do not insert an empty left remainder. The old price and its former scheduled assignment remain available at earlier recorded cutoffs. This is an audited replacement of a future schedule, not a rewrite or a backdated correction. More than one overlap, a bounded assignment or a stale expected prior still returns 409.

**Code:** yes, a small S4-02 follow-on before relying on future schedule replacement: update the publication planner and tests for equal-start success, cutoff history, retry and concurrent prior mismatch. No owner choice is needed; this enforces the packet's stated boundary.

## Q2 â€” late accepted evidence and consequence work

**Enqueue on acceptance.** Finding re-evaluation alone is insufficient: the current read already detects a changed technical digest for the *same* FindingRevision after a late accepted power interval, while migration 0011 records work only for price publication and FindingRevision insertion. A `STALE (TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED)` read is an honest safety net, not a complete recompute workflow. Record a durable, retryable work item transactionally with accepted evidence for potentially affected Site/window Findings; the worker must recheck exact role/asset/window and the latest eligible FindingRevision before deriving, so unrelated evidence can no-op. Preserve the existing FindingRevision-insert trigger for genuinely revised Findings. Deduplicate retries by accepted evidence identity and target/cause, and never append an identical consequence basis twice. The UI may say work is queued only when such a row exists; a one-shot worker still needs an explicit run/scheduling plan.

**Code:** yes, an S4-02 consequence follow-on, before S5 Overview consumes current money. It owns the migration/work selector, acceptance integration, worker idempotency and a late-power acceptance â†’ pending/stale â†’ recompute â†’ new version walkthrough. Coordinate with S2 ingestion and S4 Finding re-evaluation, but do not make those slices the sole trigger. No new owner decision is needed.

## Q3 â€” demonstration provenance

**Store provenance at ingestion.** A Site/day match to an authored spec is not proof that a particular accepted reading was authored for demonstration. The current label is acceptable for the reviewed, isolated S4-02 demonstration and its fail-closed `Source not confirmed` behavior, but it can falsely label a real KOBO-001 Finding on 2026-10-23 and is not tenant scoped. Add an immutable, tenant/Site-scoped, server-authorized batch/publication source designation with fixture/spec version and publication identity; bind it to accepted evidence IDs and carry the cited evidence's designation into Finding/consequence reads. Gateway credentials or client-declared text alone must not confer authorship. Mixed or unresolvable inputs must show a cautious source state, not claim that the whole Finding is demonstration data or real measurements. Retire the date heuristic once this path is live.

**Code:** yes, a source-provenance follow-on spanning S2 ingestion and S4 reads/UI. It must land **before any real-Site pilot and before W1 exit**; until then the current demonstration label is evidence only for the bounded S4-02 fixture, not a general source-authorship capability. **Owner input:** ask the owner to approve the visible wording for mixed/unknown provenance and the pilot data designation at the W1 checkpoint. The need for stored provenance is an architecture requirement, not conditional on that copy choice.

## Q4 â€” `assumptions:3#a` and consequence history

**Per-Finding versions do not satisfy the registered claim.** `assumptions:3#a` says *prior assumption and consequence revisions at selected cutoff* on the Assumptions interpretation-history surface. The built Assumptions view selects price history at a recorded cutoff; Overview lists consequence versions only for one selected FindingRevision, with exact price links and no consequence cutoff selection. The latter is valid `I-consequence-history-read` evidence for a per-Finding read, but it does not answer which Site consequences used a price or what the Site knew at the chosen cutoff. Exact-ID links alone do not provide that query.

**Code:** yes, an S4-02 Assumptions-history follow-on before `assumptions:3#a` promotion and W1 exit. Add a tenant/Site-scoped, paged consequence-history read at the selected recorded cutoff, with exact Finding/FindingRevision/consequence and price revision IDs, recorded/valid times, historical/current-at-cutoff distinction, and typed missing/closed-source states. frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:173:`QueryScope.window` is half-open `[start,end)` and required for analytic/product queries. `knowledge_at` makes historical audits reproducible; normal UI defaults to current server time. `selected_revision_id` freezes a drill-down even if the surrounding window changes. `AnalyticInputSet.input_sha256` hashes sorted evidence IDs **and their content digests**, resolved configuration/binding revisions, window, analytic/model version and canonical role coverage. frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:179:3. **Decide records.** In one Postgres transaction, lock batch row; for each unprocessed ordinal parse strict envelope, verify identity/sequence and referenced mapping/Foundation validity at `source_time`, normalize with the registered as-accepted conversion, and insert acceptance or rejection plus disposition. Unique message key arbitrates concurrent duplicate deliveries. Equal digest is `DUPLICATE`; changed digest is `CONFLICT` and points to first accepted evidence. Update watermark and create/coalesce recompute jobs in the same commit. Chunk a large batch into short committed transactions; receipt exposes `IN_PROGRESS` until all ordinals are durable. A client retries the same batch/bytes and resumes from the persisted watermark. Return a terminal receipt only after all decisions commit.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:183:**Initial API contract:** `POST /api/ingestion/batches` returns terminal `200` receipt or `202 IN_PROGRESS` receipt; `GET /api/ingestion/batches/{id}` returns the same durable state. `409` is reserved for same batch ID/different bytes or registered identity conflict, `422` for malformed contract, `401/403` for authentication/authorization. Normal reads use `GET /api/sites/{id}/evidence`, `/evidence/records/{id}`, `/overview`, `/performance/{view}`, `/findings/{id}` with `from`, `to` and optional `revision_id`; list reads paginate by stable `(source_time,id)` or `(created_at,id)` cursor. All responses include scope/window, revision IDs, evidence coverage and projection watermark. The UI treats a lagging projection as pending, not healthy. Lab Commit calls this same HTTP boundary with a registered simulated gateway; no privileged product-write endpoint exists.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:185:**Gateway diagnostic API:** `POST /api/gateways/{gateway_id}/diagnostics` authenticates the registered gateway/site, checks `GatewayDiagnosticsV1` identity/hash and inserts `gateway_diagnostic` with server `received_at`; an identical retry returns the existing row. `409` refuses identity reuse with different bytes, `422` malformed fields, and `401/403` wrong credential/scope. `GET /api/sites/{id}/gateway-health` returns last server contact, declared cadence, source-contact observations, queue age/depth, disk pressure, clock offset and an explicit `CURRENT|STALE|UNKNOWN` status with diagnostic ID and receive time. It makes no claim that the device or asset itself is healthy. S2-01c publishes locally; S2-02 owns central storage and read API; S7 composes the Site Health claim.

4109:Addendum to `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis` (S4-02b `fuel-cost-1`): The first reviewed fuel model may use immutable, dimensionless `sfc_upper_multiplier = 1.10` as an expressly conditional assumption that actual L/kWh does not exceed 1.10 times the selected Foundation SFC. Its version records the value, inequality, scope, source, reviewer/date, formula and immutable lineage; it is not a measured or calibrated physical bound. For each exact FindingRevision, quantify only observed Candidate spans fully covered by accepted, good, nonoverlapping generator-power mean intervals, each wholly contained within contiguous Candidate time and carrying one unambiguous positive SFC throughout. Count each distinct interval once: `quantity_low = 0 L`, `quantity_high = 1.10 × Σ(mean kW × full interval hours × SFC L/kWh)`. Never use dispatch interval `upper_minutes`, a segment `max mean × duration`, or prorating of an interval that crosses non-Candidate time. Any failed coverage, containment, power or SFC condition makes the whole consequence `QUANTITY_UNAVAILABLE` with no amount. The upper is a model-conditioned potential fuel-cost exposure, not measured fuel saved or a physical maximum. Independent model review and the planned owner UI checkpoint still apply.
